subject: reasoning
question:
By interchanging the given two signs which of the following equation will be not correct?

+ and ÷
solution:
BODMAS Rule:

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/d50192f098c21078501d30eeafe1a8c64bc30dd9621c48caa8a39ffc60f68b64.png] 

Lets check all the options 

1) 12 ÷ 8 × 12 + 6 - 7 = 21

After intechanging the signs + and ÷ , we will get,

⇒ 12 + 8 × __**12 ÷ 6**__ - 7 = 21

Applying Bodmas rule, we will get,

⇒ 12 + __**8 × **____2__ - 7 = 21

⇒ __**12 + **____**16__**__** - 7**__ = 21

⇒ 21 = 21

 

2) 9 - 3 + 12 × 8 ÷ 4 = 11

After intechanging the signs + and ÷ , we will get,

⇒ 9 - __**3 ÷ 12**__ × 8 + 4 = 11

Applying Bodmas rule, we will get,

⇒ 9 - __**0.25**____** × 8**__ + 4 = 11

⇒ __**9 - 2**____** + 4**__ = 11

⇒ 11 = 11

 

3) 46 + 23 ÷ 14 × 5 - 6 = 66

After intechanging the signs + and ÷ , we will get,

⇒ __**46 ÷ 23**__ + 14 × 5 - 6 = 66

Applying Bodmas rule, we will get,

⇒ 2 + __**14 × 5**__ - 6 = 66

⇒ __**2 + 70**____** - 6**__ = 66

⇒ 66 = 66

 

4) 6 + 20 ÷ 12 × 7 - 11 = 70

After intechanging the signs + and ÷ , we will get,

⇒ __**6 ÷ 20**__ + 12 × 7 - 11 = 70

Applying Bodmas rule, we will get,

⇒ 0.3 + __**12 × 7**__ - 11 = 70

⇒ __**0.3 + 84**____** - 11**__ = 70

⇒ 73.3 = 70, is not true

Thus, the equation **6 + 20 ÷ 12 × 7 - 11 = 70** is not correct.

Hence, the correct answer is '__**option 4**__'.
